children: Tencent Holdings' profit growth flatlined in the third quarter as surging investments in artificial intelligence eroded its bottom line.

Earnings have deteriorated in recent quarters as the Shenzhen-based company, among China's largest by market capitalization, stepped up its chip procurement this year to further advance its foundational models and various AI agent applications.

The videogame and social-media company said Wednesday that net profit edged 0.8% higher from a year earlier to 63.61 billion yuan, equivalent to $9.54 billion. Analysts had expected a net profit decline. Its adjusted net profit fell 6% to 70.55 billion yuan, roughly in line with market consensus.
Revenue climbed by a smaller-than-expected 8% to 207.34 billion yuan.
The Chinese technology titan's capital expenditure jumped more than sixfold to 81.43 billion yuan in the third quarter, which kept it in negative free cash flow.
Ahead of the results, Macquarie analysts said it expected the company's prepayments for AI chips and components to support its AI initiatives to remain a near-term cost drag.
However, recent U.S. efforts to close loopholes and deny China access to advanced AI computing, including Nvidia's chips, could complicate Tencent's efforts to expand its AI chip inventory.

"Over time, this could constrain its ability to sustain the current pace of AI infrastructure investment and potentially drag down its pace of model development and rollout of new AI applications," Nomura analysts said in a note.
The company's bread-and-butter gaming business lost some momentum in the third quarter as revenue from domestic games rose 11% while international game revenue fell 9% due to a high base.
